The environment is very calm and well curated. The minimal style works very well for this type of shop, in my opinion, as it allows the laboratory and kitchen to be visible to customers, which is always a sign of great care and quality.

The menu is not particularly extensive, which actually helps to focus on the few options available.

Coming from Donia (the owner is the same), I had no doubt that the food would be of good quality. First of all, it is a Filipino bakery and everyone working there is Filipino or of Filipino origin, so they clearly know what they are doing.
Secondly, the sando was prepared at the moment, which is great. It needs about 10 min before it being served to you.

I tried the Chicken Adobo Pocket and the Corned Beef Sando.
The first one was very good: well-made puff pastry, flavorful and tender chicken, and an optimal portion size.
The second was just as good: the meat was well cooked and tasty, the bread nicely crispy, and the sauces in the right quantity. I also appreciated the lettuce inside the sando — fresh and green. The portion was excellent here as well, although the price is perhaps just a bit slightly high for a sandwich.

The only downside is that there is not much space to place your food when sitting in front of the windows. I would probably increase the depth of the wall-mounted counter to make it easier for customers to put their food down. However, this might also be intentional to prevent people from staying too long, considering how many customers the shop receives.

Made a comeback to this café after two whole years! It’s such a famous spot that during my last visit, even though there wasn’t a queue, the terrace was completely packed, so I had to take my order to a nearby park. I still vividly remember how beautifully they packaged everything back then, which left such a wonderful impression that I just had to return!

This time, I visited on a Saturday afternoon. The staff took our order downstairs (you pay on your way out!), and we were guided to the upper floor, where we managed to snag a table. The table turnover is surprisingly quick, so people come and go pretty fast. We ordered an English Breakfast tea, scones, and a strawberry cheesecake. The scones were, as expected, absolutely legendary! Having a proper cream tea after such a long time was pure bliss. Another huge plus is that if you need more hot water or milk for your tea, you can just ask the staff, and they’ll top it up right away—we actually asked for a milk refill once. The secret to a perfect scone is the harmony between the clotted cream and strawberry jam, and their clotted cream is incredibly rich and delicious.

But the real hidden gem of the day was the almond croissant we ordered on a whim. Apparently, it’s a low-key favorite here! It was quite big, and the nutty flavor of the almonds paired perfectly with the flaky, crispy pastry. Next time I come back, ordering the scone and the almond croissant together is a non-negotiable. Plus, the atmosphere is so cozy and it’s a fantastic place for a proper catch-up. Such a satisfying visit! ☕️🧁✨

London has no shortage of great coffee shops, but ROVR stands in a league of its own.

Everything about the experience feels intentional. The interior design is warm, inviting, and beautifully considered, striking that rare balance between sophistication and comfort. Even the tableware reflects the same attention to detail.

The team are true professionals. knowledgeable, passionate, and genuinely kind. Hospitality here feels natural rather than scripted, which makes all the difference.

But above everything else, the coffee is exceptional. Thoughtfully sourced, expertly brewed, and consistently outstanding. Whether you’re ordering espresso, filter, or milk-based drinks, every cup is a reminder that you’re in the hands of people who truly care about quality.

London has no shortage of great coffee shops, but ROVR stands in a league of its own.

£20 for 50 grams of Milk Oolong, and somehow a shocking amount of that weight is stems. Not a few imperfections - actual stalks attached to nearly every rolled leaf. Apparently, at Withard, customers are expected to pay premium prices for what looks like the leftovers from tea processing.

I’ve bought Milky oolong in multiple countries, and the quality was consistently better than what this UK company is selling. Even in far less wealthy places such as Bulgaria with no tea traditions, sellers manage the basic courtesy of offering tea leaves instead of charging customers for branches... Not to mention the spoiled leaf I found amid the stalks...

For £20, I expect tea leaves — not a compost starter kit. The marketing says craftsmanship. The cup says cost-cutting with elegant packaging. Hope someone will check the quality of the batch and at least say "sorry".

When I learned that there was a coffee shop just off the beaten path in Soho that just so happens to share the name with my absolute favorite coffee drink I had to check it out.

I arrived 10min before close, so, I wasn't able to really sit in the ambiance that is Flat White. That being said, the staff was friendly, and the service was quick.

Before I talk about the drink experience, some additional details... I fell in love with flat whites when I visited Australia several years ago and I've been ordering and making them at home ever since. One thing worth noting is that a UK (and much of Europe) flat white is not quite the same as an Aussie or American flat white. It's still the same components; rich and bold espresso shot(s) accompanied by textured milk (steam milk infused with air to create a velvety texture), but in the UK they are restricted to cup sizes for some reason (mostly to do with the ratio of espresso to cup size). I was presented with a 4oz to-go coffee cup. The flavor was great, and with execution solid.

While this particular drink was delicious, I think I still prefer an Aussie flat white (or American). Having the barely bigger than espresso size feels like the drink is condensed while I want to enjoy the drink and flavor for longer.

text.text:
As of late, I think I have become a fan of the brand, not much so for the looks but for the spirit of the brand, which you can touchpoint the Aimé Leon Dore Café.

Great music curation that really sets the mood — I later found out some of it is even available online, which is a nice touch. The interior lighting is top-notch, and the private club–style design gives the space a distinct, elevated atmosphere. They also manage the number of people well, so it never feels overcrowded.

Even though the café experience is complimentary to the shop, the café is where you get to experience excellent customer service. During my time in London, I have come several times to the location. On one visit, I received a refund for a delayed coffee without even having to ask. Another time, as they were closing, they kindly offered us pastries — small gestures, but they make a lasting impression.

What stood out the most was the human interaction. The staff were genuinely likable — cool, young people who truly embody the culture and energy of the brand. We even exchanged handshakes at the end, which is the kind of personal touch you don’t get everywhere.

And one last thing, I have tried to leave a tip several times, telling them how when coming from Switzerland and working in the hospitality industry I truly value the standards they were having. I really wanted to reward their great service with a tip. I insisted but they kindly declined my request, affirming that is the kind of brand where a thank you weighs heavier than any tip.

Much respect to this team

text.text:
Overhyped, Impressive Presentation, Mediocre Flavours

I visited this establishment after seeing numerous visually appealing reels and photographs on social media. Like many others, I was drawn by its attractive aesthetic.
We ordered three items, all of which were rather average. The presentation and plating were excellent and visually striking, yet the taste fell short of the expectations created by its online popularity. The cakes were ordinary; I have had noticeably better versions from standard UK store bought cakes. The Triple Chocolate Mocha was similarly unremarkable and could easily be made at home.

Items Ordered:
1.  Triple Chocolate Mocha
2.  Double Chocolate Cake with Triple Chocolate Topping
3.  Croissants with Tomato, Cheese, and Basil

Total Bill: £26–30

It was notable that customers at the neighbouring tables also left significant portions of their orders unfinished. In addition, the seating felt quite cramped, with tables placed very close together, making movement difficult and blurring the lines between separate tables.

Conclusion:
I would not recommend this venue and would not return. It may appeal to those primarily interested in attractive surroundings for photographs, but it does not deliver a satisfying experience for those seeking quality food and comfortable dining.

text.text:
Went here craving something sweet and honestly this place delivered way more chocolate than I expected 😅 We ordered the triple chocolate cake and a hot chocolate, and both came out looking almost too pretty to eat — the cake is drizzled with three different types of chocolate (dark, milk, and white) poured right over it, and the hot chocolate cup itself was dipped in chocolate too, which was such a fun little touch.

The cake itself is dense, moist, and packed with flavor — every bite is a proper chocolate hit. The hot chocolate is thick, almost like drinking melted chocolate rather than a regular hot cocoa, which some people might love and others might find a bit much.

My only real notes — it is INTENSE, and the service was just okay, nothing special. If you're someone who prefers things on the lighter or less sweet side, the dessert might be overwhelming, and I'd definitely recommend sharing a slice between two people rather than getting your own. Staff weren't unfriendly, just a bit slow/inattentive at times, so a little more attentiveness would've made the experience better.

That said, if you're a genuine chocolate lover, this is basically dessert heaven and worth the visit just for the presentation alone. The café had a cozy, old-world feel to it, and overall it was a nice stop for anyone with a serious sweet tooth — just don't expect top-notch service to match the desserts.

Amazing if you love chocolate, slightly too rich if you don't, and service could use some improvement.

It’s one of those desserts that you try once and immediately understand why everyone keeps talking about it. Definitely worth the hype, definitely worth ordering, and without a doubt, a cake I would happily have again!

I went in today and ordered an iced latte with oat milk, ONE shot of coffee, vanilla and caramel. My friend ordered exactly the same drink. When our drinks arrived, I immediately noticed mine had been made with SEMI-SKIMMED MILK instead of oat milk — despite the fact that I have a SEVERE dairy allergy which could result in anaphylaxis. This is not a minor mistake or simply getting someone’s order wrong; this could have had extremely serious consequences.

I politely explained, saying, “I’m really sorry, but this has semi-skimmed milk instead of oat milk. I have a severe allergy to dairy.” Instead of taking this seriously, the man named Eko was incredibly rude, dismissive and actually SHOUTED in my face when I was simply trying to explain a potentially life-threatening allergy.

The drink was remade, but unbelievably, it STILL contained semi-skimmed milk and STILL had two shots instead of the one I ordered. I had to send it back AGAIN because I was understandably not willing to risk my health.

What made the situation even worse was hearing Eko say, “Why is she so picky? It’s been remade three times,” as though I was being difficult for expecting a drink to be made with the ingredients I specifically ordered — especially when one of those ingredients is related to a severe allergy.

I have never experienced customer service this appalling. Making a mistake is one thing, but repeatedly getting an allergy-related order wrong, shouting at the customer, and then mocking them for asking for it to be corrected is completely unacceptable.

I will NOT be returning unless this is properly addressed. I genuinely hope management takes this seriously, because no customer should ever be made to feel like they are being “picky” for protecting themselves from a life-threatening allergic reaction.

text.text:
If you’re hunting for a cosy English breakfast spot in Soho, KOZZEE is one of those places that instantly catches your eye with its warm lighting and chilled, rustic vibe. It feels like a proper little hideout in the middle of the city — perfect for a relaxed brunch or a quick breakfast stop.

The menu is solid, offering everything from a classic full English to pancakes, French toast, and avocado-based dishes. The coffee is definitely a highlight — smooth, well-made, and exactly what you’d expect from a central London brunch café. Some dishes, especially the French toast and breakfast plates, are genuinely enjoyable and well-presented.

Service can be a bit hit or miss. While many staff are friendly and attentive, the experience isn’t always consistent. On a good day, it feels welcoming and efficient, but at busy times it can feel slightly rushed.

In terms of pricing, it’s very much “Soho standard” — on the higher side for what you get. Some people feel the portions and quality don’t always justify the cost, especially when dishes arrive less hot than expected or seating feels cramped.

Overall, KOZZEE is a decent brunch spot with a great vibe and good coffee, but it’s not without its flaws. If you’re nearby and want a cosy breakfast experience, it’s worth a try — just go in with realistic expectations.

A great place to get some cold drinks on a specially hot day!

In a sea of bubble tea shops popping all across London, it can be difficult to choose the right one for you. I also like how the cups are easy to hold (they were thin and tall, not too chunky or thick at the bottom). All of the cup materials are reusable and recyclable which is a bonus. The staff were also polite and gave good service.

I got these 2 drinks for under £10 which was great. They also offer other drinks under this summer offer and another offer with merch, so give it a try!

I would recommend and go again ❤️

I have passed this place many times and been put off by the huge queues.

On a bank holiday, I took the chance to try it as it seemed quiet. However it turned out to be quite stressful on a hot sunny day.
As soon as you walk inside there is a till but no one was there to seve.
The kitchen looked busy and full of staff.
Then as you look to your left that is the rest of the shop, a small area to wait/collect your drink, which has the shop glass front on one side and the counter and kitchen the other. As it was a hot day, it was hot inside and then people came in to wait and collect the drinks.

There are qr codes for you to download the app to order your drinks. This really isn't great when the network  keeps dropping though.

Whilst at checkout on the app I noticed my order was rounded up and I couldnt figure out why, so I left it.
Much later I found out I was charged 20p for a paper bag which I did not need or want.

The app is good to let you know where it is in the queue and to let u know when it is waiting to be collected.
I don't believe they called out my name or number, therefore I had to collect it myself, waving down a staff member.  She was friendly and gave me my drinks.

The mangoes inside the drinks were stringy, I had to spit these out. They were not made with care.
The cups are nice and solid but seems wasteful.
It was also probably the most expensive teas we have had

Overall for us, we did not enjoy the experience of ordering and the carelessness with the mangoes, it was not worth it.

overview.text: Taiwanese bubble tea shop serving fresh milk drinks and a variety of Asian desserts.

text.text:
People say this bubble tea shop offers delicious, fresh taro milk and a wide variety of high-quality drinks and desserts, including unique soft serve ice cream flavors. They also highlight the friendly and efficient staff, noting the quick service even during busy periods.

Such a lovely bubble tea spot in Soho! The location on Frith Street is super convenient, making it the perfect place to stop for a drink while exploring or shopping around Soho.

I ordered the Brown Sugar Bubble Fresh Milk, and it was absolutely delicious. One of the best things about this place is that you can actually watch the staff prepare the drink right in front of you. Seeing them stir-fry the brown sugar together with the tapioca pearls and then add fresh milk makes the whole experience feel extra special — and the amazing smell of caramelised brown sugar fills the air!

The pearls were freshly made, perfectly chewy and coated in a rich, fragrant brown sugar syrup. Combined with fresh cold milk, the drink wasn’t overly sweet and had a really nice balance of creamy and caramel flavours.

The shop also has that cosy, familiar Taiwanese bubble tea shop atmosphere, making it a great place to sit down and chat with friends or simply grab a drink to enjoy while walking around Soho.

Definitely worth a visit if you’re a bubble tea lover!

Very disappointing experience during the buy-one-get-one-free promotion.

The store appeared severely understaffed, with nobody at the front desk when we arrived, so we had to use the self-service machine. I ordered one drink expecting the free drink to be applied automatically. After waiting for more than 10 minutes, we received only one drink and were told by a staff member, Rachael, that we had to manually add two drinks to the order for the promotion to work. She then refused to simply provide the free drink despite the buy-one-get-one-free promotion.

I asked if she could simply refund the original order so I could reorder correctly just to get that additional drink for my friend, but this was refused. There was no clear explanation of the refund policy, and nowhere on the machine, receipt, or in the store that I could see stated that drinks could not be refunded. The only no-refund notice I saw specifically concerned blind boxes.

What bothered me most, however, was not the free drink but the way the situation was handled. Rachael was dismissive and patronising throughout the interaction. At one point, she repeatedly told me to read the Chinese translation of the instructions. I am Korean, not Chinese, and I found the assumption that I should read Chinese simply because I am Asian inappropriate and uncomfortable.

When I asked for the customer service email to make a complaint, she told me that customer service would just tell me the same thing as she had, which I find dismissive and unnecessary. The email I was directed to, which she wrote on my receipt, also turned out to be invalid and went nowhere.

The ordering system seems unnecessarily inflexible, but the customer service was ultimately the bigger issue. Staff should be trained to communicate with customers respectfully and with greater cultural awareness.

I have now contacted the company through another channel and requested a refund. I will update this review if and when I receive a response.

The store appeared severely understaffed, with nobody at the front desk when we arrived, so we had to use the self-service machine. I ordered one drink expecting the free drink to be applied automatically. After waiting for more than 10 minutes, we received only one drink and were told by a staff member, Rachael, that we had to manually add two drinks to the order for the promotion to work. She then refused to simply provide the free drink despite the buy-one-get-one-free promotion.

I asked if she could simply refund the original order so I could reorder correctly just to get that additional drink for my friend, but this was refused. There was no clear explanation of the refund policy, and nowhere on the machine, receipt, or in the store that I could see stated that drinks could not be refunded. The only no-refund notice I saw specifically concerned blind boxes.

What bothered me most, however, was not the free drink but the way the situation was handled. Rachael was dismissive and patronising throughout the interaction. At one point, she repeatedly told me to read the Chinese translation of the instructions. I am Korean, not Chinese, and I found the assumption that I should read Chinese simply because I am Asian inappropriate and uncomfortable.

When I asked for the customer service email to make a complaint, she told me that customer service would just tell me the same thing as she had, which I find dismissive and unnecessary. The email I was directed to, which she wrote on my receipt, also turned out to be invalid and went nowhere.

The ordering system seems unnecessarily inflexible, but the customer service was ultimately the bigger issue. Staff should be trained to communicate with customers respectfully and with greater cultural awareness.

I have now contacted the company through another channel and requested a refund. I will update this review if and when I receive a response.

text.text:
We visited Rosa's Thai on Dean Street on a Thursday evening, and I am so glad we booked a table in advance! Even though we arrived at 6:00 PM, the restaurant was already completely packed.

It’s a fairly intimate location with about 20 tables in total, spread across the ground floor and the basement.
We were seated in the basement level right near where the food comes out. I have to admit it was a bit hotter down there than expected, though the 35°C heatwave outside certainly didn't help matters.

Despite how busy it was, the staff was exceptionally kind and patient with us.
There were so many delicious options on the menu that it took us quite a few minutes to decide, but our waitress remained attentive, friendly, and polite throughout, which we really appreciated.

To start, we took advantage of their newsletter sign-up offer and received a few complimentary small plates.
The portions were surprisingly generous and definitely large enough for two people to share.
We also decided to order the big veggie platter; however, at £20, I have to admit it felt a bit light on food for two people.
Next time, I’d probably recommend ordering one individual small starter each rather than sharing the large platter.

For our mains, I went with the classic Pad Thai. Overall, it was delicious and well-seasoned, though the tofu pieces were a little bland compared to other Thai spots I’ve tried around London.
My friend ordered the Panang Curry, which was absolutely packed with flavor and thoroughly delicious. Our main disappointment, however, was that rice isn't included with the curry and has to be ordered as an extra side. Usually, curries come with rice as standard, and given that the overall menu isn't exactly cheap, it really feels like it should be included in the price.

In total, it came out to roughly £40 per person for a main, a small starter, and a shared platter. All things considered, I’d say that’s pretty average for central London, and we had a great evening overall!

text.text:
I had the Khao Mun Gai (Chicken Rice), Roti and Iced Coffee at Rosa’s Thai on Dean Street. I’ve actually had the Khao Mun Gai twice now, and I have absolutely no notes. 🤭

The Khao Mun Gai comes with a spicy soy bean dipping sauce and chicken broth. I’ve never actually tried the dipping sauce, so I can’t tell you if it’s any good 😂, but I LOVE the chicken broth. I’m not entirely sure what the correct way to eat it is, but I pour some over the rice and chicken and then drink the rest like soup. Delicious!

I’d never had chicken prepared this way before and honestly, looks can be deceiving because it is SO tasty. The chicken is really well seasoned and the broth complements it perfectly.

The Roti was also exactly how I like it(flaky). I did wish it was a little bigger, I’m not sure sizing wise it’s worth the money. However, I also can’t make roti myself 🤭, so I’m more than happy to pay someone else to make it for me!

The only thing I wasn’t particularly impressed with this time was the Iced Coffee. I’d previously had it at the Queensway/Hyde Park location and loved it so much that I started making iced coffee like that at home. This one was much sweeter than I remembered. Once some of the ice had melted, though, it tasted much better.

It was quiet when I visited and I had no problem getting a seat. The Dean Street location has less seating compared with the Queensway/Hyde Park branch, with seating upstairs and downstairs, so I’d recommend making a reservation just to be safe.

The staff were lovely and left you to enjoy your food without hovering, which I appreciated. Overall, I’d definitely come back for that Khao Mun Gai and chicken broth!

Tried the Golden Back Cream with brown sugar pearls and really enjoyed it! The tea base was super fragrant, and the cream cheese added a nice creamy touch that balanced everything perfectly without taking away the tea flavour. It gave the drink a lot more depth and made every sip really enjoyable.

There are plenty of drinks to choose from on the menu too. The matcha series looks amazing if you're a matcha fan. If you prefer something lighter and less intense, I'd recommend the Osmanthus Oolong Milk Tea. Their classic milk tea is worth trying as well.

They also have a few seats outside, so it's a nice spot to sit back and enjoy your drink on a relaxing afternoon. And the best part? It's dog-friendly, so your furry friend can chill with you too! 🐶
